CanonicalKeywords.rationale: `{ CardKeyword.Exhaust }` (Prolong.cs:16) == `self.exhausts = True`, and crucially it is set in `_init_vars` rather than as a class attribute -- exactly so `downgrade()`'s rebuild can undo the upgrade's `RemoveKeyword`. `py tools/audit/card_probes.py downgrade` does not list prolong. The same correct pattern as card/discovery and card/gold_axe.

ctor.rationale: `base(0, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (Prolong.cs:18-21) == cost 0 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / SELF. No CanonicalVars -- the amount is the owner's current block.

OnPlay.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<BlockNextTurnPower>(choiceContext, creature, creature.Block, creature, this)` (Prolong.cs:25-26) == `if ctx.player.block > 0: PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, BlockNextTurnPower, ctx.player.block, applier=ctx.player)`. The sim's `> 0` guard is not a divergence: `PowerCmd.Apply` early-returns on `amount == 0m` (PowerCmd.cs:103), so neither side applies anything at 0 block. The block is read at play time on both sides. Presentation, folded in: the Block hover tip (14).

OnUpgrade.rationale: `RemoveKeyword(CardKeyword.Exhaust)` (Prolong.cs:31) == `self.exhausts = False`. No printed number changes on either side.
